key_facts: The remote control was designed to be a snowman shape with no LCD display, no talk-back, kinetic power, rubber buttons, and backlighting with internal LEDs.
The final design includes a jog-dial, a number pad, and the slogan incorporated into the design.
The remote control is planned to be 10 centimeters in height, with a width of approximately 3 centimeters and a depth of around 2.5 centimeters.
The remote control will not have an LCD panel or an advanced chip due to budget constraints.
The remote control will have a basic chip, four push buttons, and a single special colored button with a special form.
The remote control will be made of plastic with one special color for the case and normal colored buttons.
The remote control will have features such as brightness, contrast, color, sharpness, and sound settings.
The remote control will have a power button that can be activated by holding it for two seconds.
The remote control will have a confirm button for the LCD screen.
The remote control will have a jog-dial for volume control and advanced functions.
The remote control will have a logo, which is a Ninja Homer made in Japan, placed on the side or bottom.
The remote control was evaluated with a scoring system from 1 to 7, with the final scores being 2.5 for style, 3 for usability, 5 for soft and spongy feel, and 2 for creativity.
The team felt that the meeting environment and tools hindered creativity and collaboration.
The team suggested that using a whiteboard and having a more relaxed atmosphere would be more conducive to creative thought.
The team mentioned that the use of digital pens was clunky and hindered the flow of ideas.
The team discussed the importance of teamwork and communication, noting that they could have benefited from more in-person interaction.
The team concluded that the project was evaluated and the costs were within the budget.
The team agreed that the final design would be specified in the final report by the project manager.
